report.summary: CI/test-runtime change (split Turbo test tasks, docs-only classifier, concurrent Worker groups, phone browser project). One blocking problem: ops.test.ts makes the 'step runner rules' group describe.concurrent while one case changes the module-global STEP_LIMITS['settings.read'] to a 300 ms timeout for several seconds. Sibling cases in the same group get their setup script from settings.read at the same time, so on a loaded runner they can time out three times, fall back to defaults and never start setup. Everything else checked out: the classifier fails closed, the Turbo inputs and outputs are consistent, the browser fixtures exist, and the docs and spec are updated.

findings.text: The 'step runner rules' group is now describe.concurrent (maxConcurrency 4), but one case changes the shared STEP_LIMITS['settings.read'] to timeoutMs 300 for its whole run (3 attempts with backoff, several seconds). The DO shares that module object (the test depends on this), so concurrent siblings 'recovery after a DO restart: a running op that waits…' and 'a step's timing includes the time it waited…' run settings.read with a 300 ms timeout. Those siblings supply their setup script only through the fake settings.read reply. On a loaded runner a reply slower than 300 ms fails 3 times, the step is skipped with default settings, script.start never comes and the 'setup start' wait times out. This is a shared global under concurrent cases, against the repo rule to keep global-state groups sequential. Fix: keep this group, or this case, sequential.

evidence.why: It is inside `describe.concurrent("step runner rules", { timeout: 60_000 }, () => {`. Sibling cases run `seedWs({ effective: settingsWith({ scripts: { setup: "npm ci" } }) })`, where effective settings come only from the settings.read reply (useEffective). They then wait for `w.tempod.requestsOf("script.start").length === 1`, which never happens if settings.read times out 3 times and is skipped with defaults.

checked.risk: Tests: shared spies, globals or clock under concurrent cases; test-context expect; cleanup
Build/runtime environment: Turbo task graph (^transit instead of ^build), task inputs and outputs, fixture outDirs, scripts
Failure paths / fail closed: docs-only classification (missing, zero or invalid base, fetch failure, renames, empty diff, timeouts), workflow gating, required check kept
Tool versions: pinned oxlint/oxfmt via bunx on the docs-only path; lint config needs no node_modules plugins
Browser tests: phone project grep, tap support, fixture contracts (requests, Chose text, Back button)
Spec/docs updated with behavior change; no secrets or credentials touched
